description: Five-storey office building sprinklered throughout of noncombustible construction. The owner wants a charred solid-timber board rainscreen cladding on the street elevation. This is not a plywood-clad or other prescriptive Appendix D exterior-wall assembly. The supplier has a reaction-to-fire test from Europe but not the Canadian full-scale wall test. Can the European test support an alternative solution?
known_facts: solid timber boards rather than plywood
not a prescriptive Appendix D exterior-wall assembly

missing_info.why: Section A of the variance form

gold.departure: Combustible cladding on a building required to be noncombustible, without the CAN/ULC-S134 test result.

should_cite.why: construction requirements where openings are limited by spatial separation

gold.engineering_reason: Five-storey office is outside the exemption.

authoring.author: Batatis evaluation builder (Claude Opus 5.5)
authoring.notes: Written from the code database only; held-out judge set not consulted. Model-checked synthetic clarification on 2026-10-20: stated full sprinkler coverage and excluded the prescriptive Appendix D wall option before retaining the tested-wall benchmark.
